headline: Denmark's oldest person confirms she joined the Danish Nazi party in 1941
headline_short: Denmark's oldest was a Nazi party member
deck: Kirsten Schwalbe set the national age record on Wednesday; the broadcaster that has followed her for years says it did not know.
standard: Kirsten Schwalbe, who on Wednesday became the oldest person ever to have lived in Denmark, joined DNSAP, the Danish Nazi party, in August 1941, during the German occupation. On Friday she confirmed that she and her late husband had both been members, but would say no more.
Two historians found her in the Bovrup file, a copy of the party's own membership register published after the war.

TV Midtvest, a regional broadcaster that has followed her for four years, says it did not know. Bent Blüdnikow, a historian, told Kristeligt Dagblad that membership 'was treason', though it was not made a crime in itself after the occupation.
short: Kirsten Schwalbe, who on Wednesday became the oldest person ever to have lived in Denmark, has confirmed that she joined DNSAP, the Danish Nazi party, in 1941, during the German occupation.
